title: Interaction (I) — v1.0
description: plan.md §5.1. One per crates/*/specs/_interactions/<interaction_id>.json. #16: caller/callee, edge_class, COMPUTED eligibility (rejected on mismatch by scripts/validate_interaction.py's G1b, plan.md §5.2), rationale, evidence_links, review. #17: reliances[].required_assurance, applying §8.1's claim / evidence-method / scope / trust type split -- required_claims and accepted_evidence_kinds are separate enums with no shared values, so a bridge-checked-style value can never land in a bounded-model-check-style field. reliances is optional: an eligibility of inform/ignore has nothing to declare a reliance on, so it is never forced to an empty array. #18: realization.requirement + config_scope -- required on every interaction (unlike reliances, this applies uniformly regardless of eligibility: the issue text is 'each interaction edge declares', not conditioned on boundary-required). #19: protocol_class (plan.md §5.3) -- required on every interaction, same reasoning as realization. A non-pairwise classification requires an external protocol artifact or a reviewed protocol-debt record (docs/protocol-debt-schema.json); cross-referencing that coverage exists is G15's job, out of scope for this schema, the same boundary #16 drew for R2/exemptions.

interaction_id.description: Must equal the filename stem exactly (G1b, enforced by scripts/validate_interaction.py), same discipline as boundary_id.

eligibility.description: COMPUTED from edge_class (plan.md §5.2) -- G1b recomputes and rejects disagreement with the stored value. Never hand-set the deciding value; a proposing model cannot mark a stateful cross-verifier edge ignore.

reliances.description: What this interaction relies on from the callee, and the assurance required for each obligation (plan.md §8.1). Optional -- an inform/ignore-eligible edge has nothing to declare a reliance on.

protocol_class.description: plan.md §5.3. A non-pairwise edge is temporal/multi-step, not a simple caller-to-callee call -- it requires an external protocol artifact or a protocol-debt record (docs/protocol-debt-schema.json); a normal boundary exemption is never sufficient for it. Whether that coverage actually exists for this interaction (G15) is checked elsewhere, not here.

realization.description: plan.md §5.1: whether this edge is compiled/realized unconditionally, and the configuration it was analyzed under.

target.description: Rust target triple, e.g. x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Loosely shaped (2-4 hyphen-separated lowercase segments, each optionally dot-separated into non-empty sub-components, for targets like thumbv8m.main-none-eabi) rather than an exhaustive target list, which changes over time. Dots must sit between non-empty components -- not leading, trailing, consecutive, or adjacent to a hyphen.

obligation_id.description: <Concept>.<id>, the same shape as a boundary contract's callee_guarantees entries (e.g. TaskQueue.C003).

required_assurance.description: plan.md §8.1's type split, enforced structurally: required_claims and accepted_evidence_kinds are disjoint enums, so a claim-category value (e.g. postcondition-holds) can never be written where a verification-method value (e.g. kani-bounded-model-check) is expected, or vice versa -- bridge-checked and bounded-model-check-style values can never share a field because neither field's enum contains the other's vocabulary.

minimum_scope.description: Verifier-specific scope keys (e.g. input_domain, feature_set) -- deliberately open, since the vocabulary is not fixed across verifiers (mirrors promotion-receipt-schema.json's schema_versions).

concept.description: PascalCase, matches the concept-to-code 'concept' field convention.
